title: Shallow-Deep Networks: Understanding and Mitigating Network Overthinking
sections_checked: model and dataset setup; internal classifier placement and parameter/storage costs
confidence exit policy and oracle upper-bound results
accuracy/FLOP tables across CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny ImageNet
VGG-16/CIFAR-10 backdoor case and discussion
evidence_note: Confidence-based exits report >50% FLOP reduction on CIFAR setups and usually >25% on Tiny ImageNet without accuracy loss, but the larger 73/55/40% savings are label-aware oracle ceilings. Difficult correct cases may have lower confidence and fail to exit. Added heads increase parameter/storage cost (MobileNet example about 3.4M to 11.2M). Backdoor mitigation is one VGG16/CIFAR10 setup, not a general defense; no distribution shift evaluated.

title: Infer-EDGE: Dynamic DNN Inference Optimization in 'Just-in-time' Edge-AI Implementations
review_status: full-text section audit complete; related-version provenance checked; not independent replication
sections_checked: A2C controller, target conditions, model/split choices
Jetson/server/USRP testbed and model benchmark setup
multi-objective latency/energy outcomes and sensitivity
energy accounting, simulated mobility, workload assumptions
comparison with earlier EdgeRL arXiv version
evidence_note: Selected configurations report up to 77% lower latency and 92% lower device energy, but UAV mobility energy is simulated; video capture and server energy are excluded. Three Jetson TX2s plus server/USRP testbed; 30s slots, 3 simulated UAVs, Poisson arrivals, 4 cutpoints, 5,000 A2C episodes. Earlier 2410.12221 is a substantially overlapping related version and must not count as independent evidence.

title: Understanding the Robustness of Multi-Exit Models under Common Corruptions
sections_checked: Abstract and contributions
§3: oracle and practical confidence/patience/k-NN routes under corruption
underthinking/overthinking definitions and corruption effects
AugMix and test-time batch-normalization interventions
limitations and conclusion
evidence_note: With VGG16/ResNet56 and CIFAR-10/100-C, first-correct label-aware oracle saves ~40% compute and improves accuracy >=10%, while practical routes improve accuracy only ~1% over last exit; shift widens practical-versus-oracle accuracy gap by ~5 percentage points on average. Shift increases under/overthinking; AugMix helps tested cases. Scope is common image corruptions and two CNN backbones.

title: DART: Input-Difficulty-AwaRe Adaptive Threshold for Early-Exit DNNs
sections_checked: difficulty feature and adaptive threshold method
validation tuning and pseudo-label coefficient update
CNN, MNIST/CIFAR-10, and LeViT result tables
limitations and architecture scope
evidence_note: A100 experiments show speed/accuracy tradeoffs vary by architecture: CIFAR-10 AlexNet 82.86 vs 85.29 static, ResNet18 85.35 vs 88.32, VGG16 80.20 vs 79.16; LeViT speedups coexist with roughly 10–17 point accuracy losses in some settings. No edge-device energy validation; authors call for transformer-specific exit design. High-confidence self-pseudo-label adaptation merits validation but is not shown to fail.
